text: Celebrities make the same dating mistakes you do. I'm here to show you which ones and what you can learn. And today we're talking about the biggest YouTuber on the planet, Mr. Beast. The man who gives away millions, builds schools and wealth, and has over 400 million subscribers. But here's the thing, money, fame, success, none of that protects you from mistakes in dating. After breaking up with his ex in 2022, Mr. Beast met Thea, a South African gamer and streamer. The way it happened almost sounds like a movie. He was in Cape Town with Logan Paul and Casey Neistat, they meet a girl in a club and she later invited her friend Thea to a dinner with them. But here's the part you need to pay attention to. That encounter between Mr. Beast and Thea lasted maybe 20-30 minutes. And right away, Mr. Beast began asking her nerdy compatibility questions, which sounds more like an interview. And Mr. Beast admitted he had done this with about 40 other girls before her. And Thea was the first one who checked all the boxes. Now listen carefully, this might work for him because he's famous and rich. But for you, if you try to interview a girl when you first meet, she will probably think there is something wrong with you. Moreover, if you think that by asking her compatibility questions you would figure out if she's right for you, you are at the very least very naive. To understand if the girl is right for you, you need to spend time together, watch her actions, see her real values. And this normally takes time, because people tend to show their best parts when you first meet them, especially if you are Mr. Beast. So back to the story. After that short meeting, they part ways, but continue texting. This is where Mr. Beast decides to fly 30 hours to South Africa and 30 hours back to the US, just to see her again for one day. Sure, for him money doesn't matter, but time does. Mr. Beast says that he is very picky when it comes to girls. But let's be honest, flying 30 hours to meet a girl you met once for 20 minutes doesn't make you picky, that makes you easy. You are not showing high standards, you are showing you'll do anything for this girl's attention. So after that one-day visit, they decide to continue their relationship. But here's the complication. Thea couldn't just move to the US, she needed a visa. And if you've ever dealt with visas, you know it can be a long, frustrating process. To speed it up, they literally hired someone to refresh the visa appointment website, just so she could get an earlier slot. Now, inside of a relationship that's not a bad thing. He has money, he wants to help his girlfriend, so he used his resources. That is fair. But guys, you need to understand something. One of the golden rules of a man's life is this. Simplify, don't complicate. If you choose a girl who lives 30 hours away, who doesn't even have a visa, and who you can barely see, you are not simplifying, you are overcomplicating. For Mr. Beast, it works because he's rich, he's famous, and the girl knew being with him could mean a promising future. But for you, a long-distance relationship with all these obstacles is almost guaranteed to end badly. Don't overcomplicate your life. There are plenty of women in your city, in your country. Meet them. Create relationships that are fun, natural, and easygoing. Not ones that feel like a logistical nightmare. So here's the lesson. Don't copy Mr. Beast's love life. He can afford to test 40 girls, fall for checkboxes, fly across the world, and hire people to fix visas. But you can't. And you shouldn't. Finding the right woman is not about making things harder. It's about respecting yourself, setting standards, and keeping your life simple enough that you can actually enjoy it. Look, I hope Mr. Beast and Thea are genuinely happy together. But for you, the takeaway is clear. Don't interview women like job candidates. Don't chase after someone you barely know. And don't complicate your life with long-distance drama. Simplify. Respect yourself. And remember, money can buy flights, lawyers, even visas. But if you make wrong choices, it will never buy you peace in your personal life.
